findings.title: Test function still named after old InstrumentationMiddleware type
findings.body: The test file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the production identifier newInstrumentationMiddleware was renamed to newMetricsMiddleware, but the test function itself is still declared as `func TestInstrumentationMiddleware(t *testing.T)`. This is stale and misleading: the test now exercises the MetricsMiddleware, not an InstrumentationMiddleware, and the function name should be updated to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed type. Leaving the old name will confuse future readers, test failure reports, and any tooling that filters by test name.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no dedicated tests
findings.body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is responsible for adding the contextual logger (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) to the request context that LoggerMiddleware later reads via FromContext. Despite being a separate middleware now, there is no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go. The new code path is not exercised by any test, and the existing TestLogger helper in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go has FromContext(ctx) implemented as `return NewTestLogger()` (ignoring ctx), so even tests that use TestLogger cannot verify that the contextual attributes are actually propagated. Without coverage, regressions in the instrumentContext helper or in the middleware ordering would not be caught.

findings.title: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently drops contextual attributes on type-assertion failure
findings.body: The new FromContext implementation does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and, if the assertion fails, silently falls back to `d.New()`. The fallback returns a wrapper around a freshly created logger that has NO contextual attributes, so pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname (added upstream by ContextualLoggerMiddleware) are lost and downstream code (e.g., LoggerMiddleware logging "Plugin Request Completed") will produce log lines without the expected fields. This makes debugging harder and is a behavior change versus the previous code, where the attributes were appended directly to logParams in logRequest. The implementation should either propagate the returned logger without asserting to a concrete type, or at minimum log/return an error when the assertion fails rather than silently degrading.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger interface is a breaking change for other implementations
findings.body: The Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log is a public package and previously had five methods (New, Debug, Info, Warn, Error). This PR adds a sixth method, FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. Any type implementing this interface elsewhere in the repository or in downstream consumers (plugin SDK helpers, test doubles in other packages, third-party Grafana plugins) will fail to compile. The PR updates grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger, but does not enumerate or update other in-repo implementers. A grep for `log.Logger` implementers should be run before merge, or the interface change should be guarded with a build tag / documented as a deliberate API break in the changelog.
